skills.name: Circle vocabulary
skills.wrong_turn: A chord doesn't have to pass through the center. Only the chord through the center is a diameter.
skills.rule: Chord: a segment joining two points of the circle. Secant: a line through two points. Tangent: a line touching at one.

skills.name: Central angles & arcs
skills.wrong_turn: Arc measure isn't arc length. A 60° arc on a coin and on the equator have the same measure but very different lengths.
skills.rule: An arc's measure equals its central angle; a major arc measures 360° minus the minor arc.

skills.name: Arc length
skills.wrong_turn: Use the radius in 2πr, not the diameter. And divide the angle by 360, not 180.

skills.name: Sector area
skills.wrong_turn: A segment isn't a sector. Subtract the triangle from the sector to get the region between the chord and the arc.

skills.name: Radians
skills.wrong_turn: π is not 180. π radians equals 180°, but π on its own is the number 3.14159…
skills.rule: An angle in radians is θ=(sr); so s=rθ and sector area =(12)r2θ.

skills.name: Inscribed angle theorem
skills.wrong_turn: The vertex must be on the circle. Inside or outside it, the rule changes.
skills.rule: An inscribed angle is half the central angle on the same arc.

skills.name: Inscribed angle corollaries
skills.wrong_turn: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary, not equal. And it only works if all four corners are on the circle.
skills.rule: An angle inscribed in a semicircle is 90°; opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add to 180°.

skills.name: Tangent & radius
skills.wrong_turn: The right angle is at the point of tangency. The line from the center to the outside point is the hypotenuse, not a leg.
skills.rule: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of tangency.

skills.name: Two tangents from a point
skills.wrong_turn: Equal tangent segments come from the same outside point. Tangent pieces from different corners of a polygon are usually different.
skills.rule: Two tangent segments from one outside point are equal.

skills.name: Chord properties
skills.wrong_turn: Only the perpendicular from the center bisects a chord. A perpendicular from some other point generally doesn't.
skills.rule: The perpendicular from the center to a chord bisects it, and equal chords are equally far from the center.

skills.name: Angles from chords
skills.wrong_turn: Inside the circle, add the arcs and then halve. Don't subtract (that's for outside), and don't forget to halve.
skills.rule: Chords crossing inside a circle make an angle equal to half the sum of the two intercepted arcs.

skills.name: Angles from secants & tangents
skills.wrong_turn: Outside the circle, subtract the arcs (far minus near) before halving. Adding them is the rule for chords crossing inside.
skills.rule: Vertex outside: angle =(12)(far arc−near arc). Tangent and chord: angle =(12) the arc.

skills.name: Intersecting chord lengths
skills.wrong_turn: Multiply the two parts of each chord, not a part by the whole chord. The whole-length rule is for secants from outside.
skills.rule: Chords AB and CD crossing at P: PA⋅PB=PC⋅PD.

skills.name: Secant & tangent lengths
skills.wrong_turn: For a secant from outside, multiply the outside part by the whole secant, not by the inside part: 4 × 9, not 4 × 5.

skills.name: Equation of a circle

steps.d: graph it and find tangent lines

skills.wrong_turn: The signs flip: (x − 2)² + (y + 1)² = 25 has center (2, −1), not (−2, 1). And 25 is r², so r = 5.

skills.name: General form of a circle
skills.wrong_turn: Completing the square adds to both sides. x² − 4x is (x − 2)² − 4; forget the −4 and the radius comes out wrong.
skills.rule: For x2+y2+Dx+Ey+F=0, complete the square in x and in y.

skills.name: All circles are similar
skills.wrong_turn: π isn't 22/7 or 3.14. Those are approximations; π's decimals never end or repeat.
skills.rule: All circles are similar, so (Cd) is the same for every circle: π.
